featured_reviews.name: tanmay rao
featured_reviews.review_text:
Pratap Lunch Home is a great spot if you’re craving prawns or fish. I tried their butter garlic prawns (4/5), tawa surmai fry (4/5), and Chettinad prawn biryani (4/5). It’s a chill place with a coastal vibe and homely food—highly recommend for a quick lunch.
Top Dishes
•	Butter garlic prawns: Fresh and flavorful, hitting all the right garlicky notes without overpowering the seafood.
•	Tawa surmai fry: Crispy edges with balanced spices, showcasing the fish’s natural freshness.
•	Chettinad prawn biryani: Spicy, aromatic, and generously portioned for a satisfying coastal twist.
Vibe and Service
The relaxed, sea-inspired ambience pairs perfectly with the comforting, home-style cooking. Quick service makes it ideal for lunch breaks in the Fort area.

featured_reviews.name: Niki Mitra
featured_reviews.review_text:
Discover the flavors of the sea at Pratap Lunch Home, a hidden restaurant de fruits de mer in the heart of Fort, Mumbai! This seafood and non-veg lover's paradise is a must-visit for any food enthusiast.

The LOVE:

- Delicious Food: The dishes are packed with flavor, and the portions are generous.
- Friendly Staff: The team is attentive and welcoming, making sure you feel at home.
- Cozy Ambiance: The AC section is a blessing, especially during peak hours.
- Alcohol Served: With a 10% VAT, you can pair your meal with a drink of your choice.

Must-Try Dishes:

- Mutton Bhuna: Tender, spicy, and utterly addictive. The quantity is impressive, and the quality shines through.
- Prawns Chilly Roast: Fresh, flavorful, and perfectly cooked. A must-try for seafood lovers.

We were impressed by the food, service, and ambiance. While peak hours can get busy, the wait is worth it. We're already planning our next visit to try more of their menu offerings.

If you're a seafood or non-veg lover, Pratap Lunch Home is a must-visit destination. With its rich flavors and cozy atmosphere, it's a great spot for a night out with friends or a special occasion.

featured_reviews.name: Alwin Crasto
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had a great culinary experience having lunch here on a weekday with my family. The place was not crowded at all, the ambience was calm and inviting with a home-like touch. We came with the intention of enjoying seafood and we achieved exactly that. I definitely recommend dining here and Pratap Lunch Home is now on my must-return list!

Food we ordered:
Bombil Fry - A Bombay staple and they did it justice. (5/5)
Lobster Chilly Roast - This was my favourite. Unbelievably good! I also liked how they were transparent in showing us the sizes and prices of the lobster they had in their catch and let us choose as per our preference. (5/5)
King Prawns Ghee Roast - Also really good. (5/5)
Shell Fish Sukka - Good masala but we were not blown away. We also had to be extra careful while eating as not all hard debris were cleaned from the shell fish. (3/5)
Squid Malabar - Crispy fried squid which I couldn't get enough of. (5/5)
Prawns Vijaywada - Decently flavoured prawns curry. (4/5)
Mutton Tawa Pulao - I've never had pulao done so well. Good sized portion too. (5/5)

featured_reviews.name: Saquib Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Central Lunch Home, nestled in the vibrant neighborhood of Cuffe Parade, stands out for its delectable seafood offerings and authentic Mangalorean cuisine. One of their standout dishes is the Bombil Fry, a crispy delight that perfectly balances the delicate flavors of the fish with a tantalizing blend of spices. Each bite offers a satisfying crunch, making it an absolute must-try for seafood enthusiasts.

Another gem on their menu is the Mangalorean Style Chicken Sukkha, a rich and aromatic dish that bursts with flavors. The tender chicken pieces are marinated in a blend of traditional spices, cooked to perfection, and then simmered in a luscious coconut-based gravy. It's a dish that showcases the culinary prowess of Central Lunch Home's chefs and keeps patrons coming back for more.

For those looking for a hearty and fulfilling meal, the Egg Masala is a top choice. This dish features boiled eggs cooked in a flavorful masala gravy, infused with spices that pack a punch. It's a comforting dish that pairs well with rice or bread, making it a favorite among diners.

One of the most appealing aspects of Central Lunch Home is its affordability. Despite offering high-quality seafood and authentic dishes, the prices remain reasonable, making it accessible to a wide range of customers. Additionally, the portion sizes are generous, ensuring that diners leave fully satisfied.

However, it's worth noting that Central Lunch Home can get quite busy during peak hours, which might result in longer wait times. Nevertheless, the bustling atmosphere adds to the charm of the place, creating an authentic dining experience.

In summary, Central Lunch Home at Cuffe Parade is a haven for seafood lovers and aficionados of Mangalorean cuisine. With its affordable prices, generous portions, and high-quality food, it's no wonder why this restaurant is a favorite among locals and visitors alike. Whether you're craving Bombil Fry, Mangalorean Style Chicken Sukkha, or Egg Masala, Central Lunch Home delivers on taste, making every visit a memorable culinary adventure.

So I obliged and waited outside for my parcel for a while, until the polite guards at the gate asked me why are you waiting, so I told them that I have made an order and that the receptionist told me to wait outside. They felt almost embarrassed that I was waiting outside and told me to get in and sit. Very grateful to them as I went inside and sat down on the sofa. After a while, the waiter came with my order and provided me the bill, I checked as it said 240 including gst which became 252. Got the correct change and I left. But when I checked Zomato, I noticed that the price of a chicken biryani is 210 and for 240 one can get Chicken Tikka Biryani. I found that a bit strange since I didn't eat inside and just got my order and left. Anyways, I thought I should share with you because I felt the receptionist's behaviour was quite rude. featured_reviews.name: Gaurav Biswas
featured_reviews.review_text:
Waited for 15 minutes to get a place.
They serve all sorts of packet Chaknas here like Moong Dal, Chakli, Seng, Chana, Roasted Chana Etc. These are all reasonably priced between 20 to 40.

We order Bombil Fry, Chicken Sukka, Kori Rotti and Neer Dosa & Solkadi
Being married to a Mangalorean and been a regular to Mangalorean outlets back in Kudla I know the taste very well. This was nowhere near sadly. The Bombil Fry being a Maharashtrian special was just oil fried with light red batter rather than Rawa Fry. Killed the appetite completely unfortunately. It was served a small bowl of Coconut gravy which was again very bland.

The Chicken Sukka was too bland. Quantity was ample but the taste was honestly bland. I tried to finish it with the Neer Dosa since Bhakri wasn't available.

Neer Dosa again was served with a small bowl of Coconut gravy as usual bland.

The Kori Rotti being a staple food amongst mangaloreans was a major let down. It didn't have any flavor and even had sasive(Mustard) in it which was unlike of any Mangalorean Outlet. My wife finished it with a lot of difficulty.

The only savior was the Solkadi and it was really tasty and thick. It was too good and cheap at the same time.

Overall verdict is it's a cheap and pocket friendly place. The food was 2/5. Drinks are probably cheap since everyone was busy consuming that. Solkadi 6/5. The staff were always on the feet and ready to attend.

Just experienced a fantastic meal at the iconic Bharat Excellensea, a 35-year-old gem in Mumbai's Ballard Estate! The restaurant has been recently revamped, and the ambiance is now even more inviting. But the real star is the food!

As a self-proclaimed seafood addict, I was in heaven. I sampled a wide range of dishes, each bursting with flavor and freshness.

The Tom Kha Soup was a fragrant and comforting start. The Prawns Butter Garlic were perfectly cooked and incredibly flavorful. The *Yellow Chili Prawns  packed a delicious spicy punch. The Surmai Masala Fry was a classic done exceptionally well. The Thalasseri Clams were a fiery delight, showcasing the flavors of Kerala. The Rawas Gassi was a rich and creamy Mangalorean-style curry. The Neer Dosa and Appam were the perfect accompaniments to soak up the delicious gravies.

But the real surprise was the Sitaphal Tricones Holige! This innovative dessert was a delightful fusion of Indian and modern flavors. A must-try!

Overall:
Bharat Excellensea is a must-visit for any seafood lover in Mumbai. The restaurant offers a wide variety of fresh, flavorful dishes with influences from across India's coastal regions. The recent revamp has enhanced the dining experience, making it a perfect spot for a special occasion or a memorable meal. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Debabrata Golder
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you are a seafood lover looking for an authentic and budget-friendly meal near Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CST), Sandeep Gomantak Hotel is an absolute must-visit.
Getting There & Parking
The restaurant is incredibly convenient if you are traveling by train, located just a short 5 to 7-minute walk from the CST station. I highly recommend that you go by walk only. Because it is situated in a bustling, crowded area, there is absolutely no parking available. Trying to find a spot for your vehicle nearby is a major problem and will only add unnecessary hassle to your meal, so walking is definitely the smartest option.
Ambiance & Service
Despite being a busy eatery, the management does a great job of maintaining the space. The dining area is kept very neat and clean, making for a comfortable environment to enjoy your meal. Additionally, the service is impressively fast. The staff is efficient and attentive, ensuring you get your food quickly even during peak lunch or dinner hours.
The Food
The star of the show here is undoubtedly the authentic Konkan-style cooking. The fish items are perfectly spiced, incredibly fresh, and exceptionally tasty. What makes it even better is that everything is well under budget, offering fantastic value for money without compromising on flavor. If you visit, you absolutely must try the crab—it is wonderfully prepared and easily one of the standout dishes on the menu.
Verdict
Overall, Sandeep Gomantak offers a fantastic, no-frills dining experience that hits all the right notes for coastal food cravings. Fast service, clean surroundings, and mouth-watering seafood make it a true hidden gem. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Daddyslittlelunchbox
featured_reviews.review_text:
Mahesh Lunch Lounge was an absolute standout and easily one of our best meals in India. We chose to eat here over the Taj after it was strongly recommended by locals — and we are so glad we listened. From start to finish, the experience was fantastic.

The food was exceptional, especially the seafood. The tiger prawns were MASSIVE — genuinely some of the biggest prawns we’ve ever seen, let alone eaten. They were cooked perfectly, full of flavour, and without doubt the best prawns we had in India. That’s saying something, especially as we truly believed Kerala couldn’t be beaten when it came to seafood.

Service was attentive and efficient without being overbearing, and the prices were surprisingly good for the quality and portion sizes. One bit of advice: order your starters before committing to mains — the portions are generous and we definitely over-ordered because everything sounded too good to miss (no regrets, just very full 😅).

Overall, Mahesh Lunch Lounge completely lived up to the hype and then some. Incredible food, huge portions, great service, and excellent value. If you’re debating where to eat — go here.

featured_reviews.name: Adil Syed
featured_reviews.review_text:
Location & Popularity
Bagdadi is located in a prime area of Colaba, making it easily accessible and always buzzing with people. The restaurant is extremely popular, especially during evening hours, which clearly reflects its strong reputation among food lovers.

Waiting Time
Due to the heavy rush during peak hours, particularly in the evenings, customers usually have to wait for their turn. While the wait can be a bit long, it also speaks volumes about how loved the food here is.

Food Quality
The food at Bagdadi is genuinely great. The flavors are rich, consistent, and worth coming back for. It’s one of those places where the taste truly lives up to the hype.

Ambience & Renovation (Personal Opinion)
In my personal opinion, the restaurant could really benefit from a renovation. The place feels a bit dated, and a refresh would greatly enhance the dining experience without taking away from its old-school charm.

Final Verdict
Bagdadi is a must-visit for its excellent food and prime Colaba location. Despite the waiting time and the need for renovation, the taste and authenticity make it well worth the experience—especially for those who don’t mind a little wait for good food.

Let's start with the 40 minute wait. When you're made to wait that long, you naturally expect something rewarding at the end of it...The ambience was good, and after waiting so long to get a table, we were genuinely happy to finally be seated. The place is moderately expensive, and honestly, nobody mind paying a premium if the experience justifies it. Unfortunately, the service here was pathetic

My friend asked for a bottle of water and specifically requested one at normal temperature. Even after more than 30 minutes, it didn't arrive. When it finally did, they brought chilled water instead. I understand weekends are busy and service may take longer than usual, but taking that much time for a simple bottle of water is ridiculous

Not wanting to waste any more time, we ordered Masala Papad. When it arrived, it had no sev on it. Upon asking, we were casually told that they didn't have available. At the prices you're charging, are customers supposed to simply accept a poorer experience without question?

Then came the next masterpiece. One of my friends ordered a Diet Coke. After waiting more than 10 minutes, the waiter brought a regular Coke. At that point, all of us started laughing because it had become almost comical. When we asked whether they even had Diet Coke, he confidently said they did. The problem was that he had already opened the regular can before asking to change it.

Unfortunately, the experience didn't stop there. We ordered Tandoori Rotis, and the first round arrived burnt to the point that they looked like coal. We told the waiter and politely requested that the next be made properly. The second round arrived looking exactly the same. When we pointed it out, the waiter simply replied, "Weekend hai sir, ho jata hai"

For God's sake, man, we're here to enjoy our weekend too. Why are you ruining the experience?

Throughout the evening, we kept laughing at all the things that kept going wrong because otherwise it would have been frustrating. But when the bill arrived, I genuinely felt compelled to write this review. I rarely leave negative reviews and have never written one this harsh before, but this experience left me with no choice :,)

featured_reviews.review_text:
Located at Colaba Causeway, this mughlai place is a pretty old and one of the legendary eateries which the city has to offer

The place has a royal ambiance but i believe they are definitely in a need of upgrade now.. especially the upper floors. The service is good.. initially it took a while for them to serve us as there was a huge corporate group having their party but once they had their attention to us.. they made sure that we are served well!

We went there for lunch, we ordered:
1) Roomali Roti: The roti was literally soft like a cushion and melts in your mouth, this is one of the best Roomali roti I have ever had.

2) Chicken Bhuna: Made on tawa, this boneless chicken bhuna was actually delicious. Chicken cooked was soft and melting in my mouth whereas the masala had right amount of spices to it and wasn't spicy which was to my liking!

3) Chicken Tikka Biryani: Usually the highlight of the restaurant, but to my surprise the biryani was better than what I had 1.5 years ago as it seems their chef has changed. The last time when I had it, the chicken was really dry and had been marinated in red color.. though it was charred well but was too dry! Whereas this time the tikka was properly marinated and grilled to the right amount leaving the chicken juicy and tender. The quantity served was good too. The rice i believe could have been more fluffier.

4) Sweet Fresh lime soda: The lemon concentrate at the bottom mixed with sugar and added soda.. mixed well.. definitely was refreshing but i wish they could add the fresh lemon juice for better taste.

Overall, a good place to have your fulfilling dinner.. the place had originally introduced to me by my mother.. though it might have changed over the time but still manages to have the same pull!

featured_reviews.name: Janhavi Raut
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Goankar Cuisine in Mumbai, and overall it turned out to be a mixed but interesting dining experience. When we first arrived, the restaurant was completely empty, but as we started ordering, the place quickly became busy and was soon filled with many guests.

We began with crab Manchow soup, but honestly it tasted more like a regular Manchow soup as the crab quantity was very minimal and there wasn’t much seafood flavour in it. After that, we tried prawns lollipop, which unfortunately was not good. The texture felt sticky and unusual, and it was difficult to even recognize the prawns properly, so we didn’t enjoy that dish.

However, the experience improved with the next dishes. The squid Koliwada was excellent — very crunchy and perfectly cooked. It was definitely one of the better starters we tried.

The staff member Mr. Akash, who was serving us, was very helpful and gave good suggestions. On his recommendation, we tried chicken Kalakari, which turned out to be really tasty. It had a rich, authentic Indian-style chicken masala and was well marinated with great flavour.

For the main course, he first suggested chicken vindaloo, but since it is slightly tangy, we decided not to order it. Instead, he recommended chicken Xacuti (Shakoti), which was excellent and full of authentic Goan flavours. Along with that, we tried prawns masala dry, which was honestly amazing and one of the highlights of the meal.

We paired the dishes with Amboli, Ghavna, and rice bhakri. The rice bhakri was very large and quite filling, making it a great accompaniment to the curries.

For dessert, we tried Ukdiche Modak ice cream, which was truly a game changer. It was such a unique dessert that we ended up ordering another one because everyone at the table loved it. It was a really creative and delicious twist on the traditional modak.

Overall, despite a few disappointing starters, the main course, dessert, and the helpful service by Mr. Akash made the experience really enjoyable. If you visit, definitely try the squid Koliwada, prawns masala dry, chicken Xacuti, and the Ukdiche Modak ice cream.

featured_reviews.name: priyanka mustafi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Good food, quite authentic in taste. We had prawn manchow soup which was loaded with prawns. Their prawn lollypops are great, we also had squid tawa masala which was a bit salty but well cooked. We ordered thalis which was the main aim. Surmai and pomfret. The size was very good and fish was fresh. The thali was very good - rice, bhakri ( u can choose amboli or even chapati) , bhurji, sukka, prawn curry, bangda curry, salad and ofcourse rawa fry of the fish you choose. The place is very tiny with only 8 tables but service is prompt and nice ambience for a homely meal
.

featured_reviews.name: Vinayak Moorthy
featured_reviews.review_text:
Goaikar – where the fish is larger than life and the flavours come with a warning ⚠️🐟

Walked into Goaikar with big Goan expectations and walked out with an even bigger respect for their humongous fish portions. Let’s start with the clear winners of the day — the prawns lollipop and the stuffed bombil fry. Absolute show-stealers. Crisp, juicy, perfectly seasoned… the kind of dishes that make you nod silently while chewing because words fail you.

Next up, the iconic Goan ros omelette with poee — decent, comforting, but didn’t quite give us that nostalgic roadside Goan punch. More “okay okay” than “arre waah”.

Now to the grand thali saga 🍽️
We ordered the Surmai fish thali, Pomfret special thali, and Bombil thali — and oh my God, the fishes were MONSTERS. Fried to golden perfection, fresh, meaty, and clearly not shy about their presence on the plate. Total paisa-vasool when it comes to the fish itself.

But (there’s always a but)… the accompanying curries and gravies came in hot — and not the fun kind 🌶️🔥
For us, especially with a Goan mom in the house, the gravies felt too spicy and a little off-track from traditional Goan flavours. More fire, less finesse. Authentic Goa whispered… while chilli shouted.

Just when our taste buds were waving a white flag, dessert arrived like a saviour from heaven — Ukdiche Modak Ice Cream 🍨✨
Sweet, comforting, innovative, and honestly the icing on the cake (or modak on the ice cream?). A perfect, soulful ending that brought smiles back instantly.

From a value standpoint, pricing sits firmly at the premium end, with most dishes priced at ₹500 and above. While the generous seafood portions partially justify this, the ukdiche modak ice cream, though innovative and flavourful, was served in a modest portion at ₹180, feeling more like a tasting than a finale.

It is also worth noting that several social media claims suggesting a 10% discount at the restaurant did not reflect our experience, and no such concession was available during our visit—something diners may wish to verify in advance.

What truly elevated the experience was the service. Our order taker, Aditya, was exceptionally warm, attentive, and knowledgeable, guiding us with genuine enthusiasm. The entire service team mirrored this standard—courteous, efficient, and consistently welcoming—adding a layer of hospitality that made the meal feel relaxed and well cared for.

Final verdict:
Goaikar nails seafood portions and frying like a boss, experiments boldly with flavours, and redeems everything with dessert magic. A must-visit for fish lovers — just keep a glass of water (and an open mind for spice) handy 😄🔥🐠

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (minus half a star for the chilli ambush)

We had ordered Prawns biryani, Pomfret thali and Egg Masala. The Biryani was too good. The  Thali and Egg Masala was also very Delicious. The Solkadi was too good.
The Food is prepared fresh on order so may be that's the reason the food takes bit  long time to come but Quality of Food is very good and Fresh.
They accept only order through Food delivery apps or walkin and takeway.

featured_reviews.name: Akash Kargutkar
featured_reviews.review_text: Extremely disappointing experience. For a place claiming to serve Maharashtrian cuisine, the flavors were completely missing—bland and unauthentic. To make matters worse, the portions are tiny and definitely not worth the high price tag. I left hungry and regret spending money here. Avoid this place if you want a real meal.

featured_reviews.review_text: Good food.. the restaurant is slightly small so it's better to have a reservation before you go there. But the food, service and hygiene is excellent.

featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
"An absolute hidden gem for Malvani food lovers in Borivali! Run by a wonderful Marathi couple, this place truly brings the authentic taste of Konkan to Mumbai at very pocket-friendly rates. I highly recommend trying their Halva Mini Thali and Tisre Thali—they look super tempting and taste even better. The secret to their incredible taste is their spices, which are sourced directly from the Konkan region. The owners also maintain excellent quality and hygiene. Highly recommend visiting to enjoy some fantastic food and support a great local Marathi business!"

featured_reviews.name: Prathamesh Bandivadekar
featured_reviews.review_text: Visited Taste of Konkan in Borivali and had a wonderful experience. We tried the Kolhapuri Mutton Thali, Surmai Fish Thali and Stuffed Bombil Fry and every dish was packed with authentic flavours. The mutton was perfectly cooked with a rich, spicy gravy, while the Surmai was fresh and served in a generous portion. The Stuffed Bombil Fry was crispy and absolutely delicious. The ambience was warm and welcoming, making the overall dining experience even better. Definitely a great place for anyone looking to enjoy authentic Konkani food in Mumbai!

They offer both veg and non-veg options and start you off with a refreshing Kokam Sarbat. Highly recommended for authentic flavors!

featured_reviews.name: Vikram Shirodkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Taste of Konkan 🐟✨
Fair prices, authentic Konkani flavours, and a warm welcome with kokam sarbat & papad 👌
Surmai thali (₹700) stole the show with 3 crispy fried pieces 🤌

featured_reviews.name: Aditi Prabhu
featured_reviews.review_text:
Ambiance: Simple, soothing, with both indoor and outdoor sitting. Located at Babhai Naka, Borivali.

Our experience: We went in for dinner on a weekday. The place was largely empty and quiet. Took them 20 mins to take our first order despite having only 4 tables being served including ours.

We ordered the following dishes:
• Bombil Fry: The coating was way too thicker and the bombil hardly present. Could barely taste the bombil.
• Prawn koliwada: Again the coating overpowered the flavor of prawns.
• Bangda Thali and Ravas thali: Both thalis were exactly the same with the same fish curry, a tiny serving of prawn preparation, another tiny serving of matki usal in one thali and another random gravy in the bangda thalis. We weren't asked about our preferences for wada, chapati or bhakri. So one thali came with wadas, the other with chapati and on placing the order the third, we were asked about our preference for chapati or bhakri then informed bhakri is probabaly over. So we okayed chapati but were served wadas.

We also ordered another plate of extra chapati which they didnt have and offered wadas but none reached our table even after 2 reminders.

Finally we finished our meals and then asked for the bill which had the extra cost of wadas which we ordered and never recieved and also for the wada in thali which we weren't informed were charged extra but were given as they didnt have chapatis or bhakris.

They did change the bill on being informed.

We also asked for regular water which we recieved almost at the end of the meal after being reminded for the fifth time.

Service: Slow, and confused even when there were just 2-3 tables with people only.

While we understand it was end if the day and hence the food there was over and also probably that is why there were many errors & delays in service. But the overall experience and food were not upto the mark or hype.

featured_reviews.name: anish tatkare
featured_reviews.review_text:
Today I went to this hotel with my family for a dinner.
The hotel's name is only Taste of Konkan, but there is no taste of Konkan anywhere. I'm from Konkan. So don't fool people by talking about the taste of Konkan.
The chicken thali only had the taste of Elaichi and nothing else. Same with Prawns thali too. Bombil Bhaji was of a lower standard than Onion Bhaji.

featured_reviews.name: Tejas Khandalekar
featured_reviews.review_text: We enjoyed the food. Prawns thali and Kombadi vade was great options which we enjoyed. Prawns curry, Prawns masala was so delicious. Sol kadhi was also tasty. In kombadi vade, curry was perfectly Malvani taste and vade was crunchy and yummy. However, bombil bhaji (pakoda) was not that great. Overall food was good, ambience was also good

name: Aapla Samadhan
description:

While our main focus remains on delivering the bold, authentic tastes of Malvani coastal cuisine—from our signature seafood dishes to our famous Malvani thalis—we’ve also expanded our menu to include a variety of Chinese dishes, blending the best of both worlds to satisfy every craving. Whether you're here for the spices of the coast or the flavors of the East, Samadhan promises an unforgettable dining experience.

featured_reviews.name: Chetan Poojari
featured_reviews.review_text: A surge of positive reviews on social media and glowing Google ratings initially drew me to this restaurant. I was genuinely excited to try the local Malvani cuisine for lunch. However, my enthusiasm quickly waned the moment I tasted the Bombil Rava fry, it was disappointing and lacked the freshness I expected. We also ordered the Pomfret Thali and Mutton Thali, but both dishes fell short of standards, displaying a strong, unpleasant odor and stale flavors. Based on this experience, I strongly advise against visiting if you truly appreciate authentic Malvani food, as there are many better options available nearby.
